comments.text: 作者 XDGEE (XDGEE) 看板 movie 標題 [新聞]《英雄內戰》黑寡婦為何不加入美國隊長？ 時間 Thu May 7 23:41:30 2026 《英雄內戰》中黑寡婦為何不加入美國隊長陣營？原因正式揭曉！ 在慶祝《美國隊長3：英雄內戰》上映10週年的紀念活動中， 導演喬·羅素與安東尼·羅素親自解開了影迷懸掛十年的疑問：為 什麼與隊長交情深厚的黑寡婦，最後卻選擇站在鋼鐵人這邊？ 這部於2016年5月6日上映的巨作，集結了克里斯·伊凡、史嘉蕾·喬韓 森與小勞勃·道尼等超強卡司。喬·羅素在接受《CBR》專訪時透露， 娜塔莎最初確實是被設定在美國隊長的陣營，「在早期的劇本草 稿中，娜塔莎站在史蒂芬那一邊是很顯而易見的，事實上我們也是這麼寫的。」 然而，導演們隨後發現這個決定無法給予黑寡婦足夠強烈的角色視角。 喬·羅素解釋道：「問題在於，我們覺得她只是在附和隊長的觀點。 當我們把她移到東尼陣營時，反而放大了她在這部電影中的主體意識與觀點。」 喬進一步分享了幕後創作的心法：「我們最終追求的，一是如何帶給觀眾最大的驚喜， 二是如何產生最強烈的衝突與最豐富的故事。」 羅素兄弟將《英雄內戰》形容為一場「長達10年的情感投資」， 並感性地表示他們與觀眾之間存在著一種超乎想像的情感連結。 https://www.superherostar07.com/archives/27191 --

comments.text: 作者 XDGEE (XDGEE) 看板 movie 標題 [新聞]克里斯伊凡回歸《復仇者5》不演美國隊長！ 時間 Wed Dec 24 23:49:00 2025 克里斯伊凡回歸《復仇者5》不演美國隊長！ 當地23日，導演羅素兄弟首次談到美國男演員克里斯‧伊凡回歸 《復仇者聯盟5》，還傳出他將扮演遊牧者。 至於這部漫威電影與《沙丘3》同日上映會影響票房嗎？據傳華納兄弟影業對撞期一事鐵了心不讓步。 導演羅素兄弟22日在社群媒體IG上放上克里斯‧伊凡（Chris Evans）飾 演的前美國隊長史蒂芬‧羅傑斯將回歸《復仇者聯盟5：末日崛起》 （Avengers: Doomsday）的預告片，並寫道：「那個 改變我們一生的角色，那個把我們都聚在一起的故事，終究還是會回到 這裡……」片中可以看到羅傑斯把美國隊長的戰袍放進盒子裡了。 據《ComicBookMovie》報導，23日，漫威內部人士亞歷克斯‧佩雷斯 （Alex Perez）透露（點這）， 「我很高興大家能聚在一起討論這件事， 我趁機把一件事講清楚。《復仇者聯盟5》會有美國隊長出現，他 就是山姆‧威爾森，由安東尼‧麥基（Anthony Mackie）飾演。 克里斯‧伊凡會回歸演史蒂芬‧羅傑斯，但他不會披上美國隊長的戰袍。」 至於羅傑斯的新稱號是什麼？19日，好萊塢內幕人士傑夫‧史奈德（ Jeff Sneider）透露（點這）說，「就像我一年前講的，他不是真的 回來當美國隊長。就連預告片也只說：『史蒂芬‧羅傑斯將回歸《復 仇者聯盟5》。』並沒把他定位成美國隊長。原本的遊牧者（Nomad） 就是羅傑斯放下美國隊長制服跟頭銜後，換上的另一個身份。」 另據《ComicBookMovie》《The Direct》報導，除了《復仇者聯盟5》 首支前導預告片釋出外，「雷神索爾」將會是第二支預告片的主角， 原本第三支預告片將聚焦「洛基」，第四支展示「末日博士」。但據史奈德23 在節目中透露，第三支其實會聚焦在X戰警，而第四支則會主打驚奇4超人跟瓦干達人。 那觀眾還會看到末日博士？據報導，漫威剪輯了多支《復仇者聯盟5》的預告片， 或許還能在這些宣傳片中看到這個角色的身影，但史奈德認為漫威影業 打算盡量把這反派藏起來，盡量不露臉。所以，這波宣傳順 序很合理的：先推羅傑斯跟雷神，代表原本的地球最強英雄， 接著再來其他團隊，大家團結起來對抗末日博士以及他的軍團。 除此之外，《復仇者聯盟5》將於2026年12月18日在美國上映，這與《沙丘3》（Dune: Part Three）的上映日同一日。對此，史奈德表示，他的消息來源堅稱《沙丘3》不會更改上映日期。而據前《好萊塢報導者》編輯馬修‧貝羅尼（Matthew Belloni）在節目中也透露，華納兄弟已經重申立場，宣稱是他們先確定這個日期，鐵了心不讓步。 但據《DarkHorizons》報導，撞期有一個大問題就是IMAX銀幕。《沙丘3》會優先考慮IMAX銀幕，因為新任攝影師是用新一代IMAX攝影機拍。而羅素兄弟之前曾表示希望《復仇者聯盟5》能推出IMAX版本，但最終能否實現，就讓觀眾拭目以待囉。 https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/25/12/24/n14661432.htm --

comments.text: 'Captain America: Brave New World' came close to pleasing me, but in the end I think it is not consistently enjoyable enough to be classed as something I'd want to watch again and/or recommend. There is quite a bit about it that I did like, but the down moments hurt the ups. The cast and their characters are positives. I'm a big fan of Anthony Mackie's as he has done many roles in films that I've highly, highly enjoyed; interestingly, he has appeared in three of the fourteen films I've given a total 10/10 to. Here, he is very good in the titular part. I'm not someone overly attached to Marvel and therefore Chris Evans' Captain America, so this new era doesn't hinder my interest in the lead character. I'm admittedly not wholly convinced Mackie is undoubtedly a perfect fit for the role, though his performance itself is perfectly watchable and fun enough. Carl Lumbly's performance as Isaiah is great in this, he genuinely made me care quite a bit about Bradley; especially in the more emotive scenes. Danny Ramirez, Harrison Ford, Giancarlo Esposito (a little typecast still, sadly) and Tim Blake Nelson (albeit the weakest) are also pluses that I have for this movie. My main issues lie with the plot and how it is told. There were too many moments where I could feel myself losing interest in events onscreen, most notably across the first half. The second half is better paced, if still not making for superb viewing. I was firmly awaiting the credits, which is never a good sign. When I was locked on to the story, I did dig it. I particularly found the interactions/dynamics between characters to be solid, for example Cap with Carl, Joaquin and Seth. I just think what lets this down, unfortunately to a somewhat damaging degree, is that the plot just isn't quite good enough. A shorter run time (even though it isn't that long) may have helped, but I'm not sure. I just realised that this is the first MCU film that I've scored below 7/10. That feels harsh

comments.text: “Brave New World” but same old yarn, sadly. Morgan Freeman clearly didn’t fancy this one so Marvel have resurrected another ex-president in Harrison Ford to put together a treaty that will deliver the old save the globe type of thing. It’s all about this giant hand-shaped structure that has emerged from the ocean and that contains “adamantium” - and that’s even more indestructible than “Vibranium” (how can something be more indestructible?). Anyway, before this accord can get signed off by a curious quadrumvirate of the USA, India, France and China a shipment of this new material gets pinched and it’s down to “Capt. America” (Anthony Mackie) and his new sidekick “Torres/Falcon” (Danny Ramirez) to retrieve it. Loads of end-to-end fisticuffs later and the goods are secure which earns our dynamic duo and their inspirational trainer “Bradley” (Carl Lumbly) an invitation to the White House. That’s where the wheels really do come off as their pal starts taking potshots at the President and we discover that the erstwhile somewhat militaristic and temperamental “Ross” and “Cap” aren’t exactly on the same page. It’s pretty obvious that there’s a third party pulling the strings so it’s going to need all of his patience and guile if the shielded wonder is to retrieve his mentor from solitary, rebuild his relationship with his president before that man really sees red, and also get to the bottom of a dastardly scheme that seems bent on causing international strife between the USA and Japan.
